title: Adaptive Quant Evaluation Protocol and Triage
author: Priya Raman
body:
Summary

This document defines Redwood's Adaptive Quant Evaluation Protocol (AQEP): a reproducible, cohort-driven evaluation and rollout practice that links quantization profile selection to targeted prompt cohorts, runtime guardrails, and a rapid regression-triage path. AQEP is designed to minimize unit-cost risk from quantized model variants while preserving end-user quality across diverse workloads.

Goals

- Provide a single, auditable protocol for evaluating quantized candidates before production rollout.
- Tie evaluation signals to the same prompt cohorts used in production quality monitoring.
- Specify canary, rollback, and triage steps to reduce MTTR for quantization regressions.
- Ensure instrumentation and thresholds are consistent across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Scope

- Applies to transformer-based encoder-decoder and decoder-only models that Redwood serves via the runtime.
- Covers INT8 and 4-bit quantization profiles and mixed-precision variants.
- Integrates with the Eval Harness, Prompt Cohort Catalog, Quality Guardrails, and Regression Triage runbooks.
- Excludes custom model architecture changes and retraining (handled by model onboarding).

Key Definitions

- Prompt Cohort: A labeled grouping of prompts/requests representing a stable slice of production traffic (e.g., "short-instructions", "multi-turn-chat", "code-completion-ml").
- Quant Candidate: A model binary produced by a quantizer pipeline and labeled with a quant profile (e.g., q4f16-ld).
- Delta Metric: Relative change between baseline (float/bf16) and quant candidate for a metric (e.g., delta_exact_match = (q - baseline) / baseline).
- Canary Window: Timeframe and traffic percentage used for staged rollout (default 4 hours, 1% traffic).

Cohort Construction and Responsibilities

1) Cohort Cataloging
- Ownership: Applied ML team + Product Metrics.
- Each cohort entry must include: name, description, canonical prompts (10–200 examples), selection predicate (traffic filter), and intended functional coverage.
- Example cohort metadata (text table):

  | Name                 | Predicate                                  | Examples | Owner          | Notes |
  | short-instructions   | tokens < 40, system_prompt = null            | 50       | applied-ml     | high volume |
  | multi-turn-chat      | conversation_turns >= 3                      | 40       | customer-eng   | dialog context |
  | code-completion-ml   | language = python and prompt contains 'def'  | 30       | devx           | critical correctness |

2) Cohort Refresh
- Refresh cadence: quarterly by default, or after a model-major release.
- Triggered refresh after significant drift (10% traffic distribution change) or new feature launches.

Eval Harness Integration

- The Eval Harness must execute the following pipeline for each Quant Candidate:
  1. Load baseline float model and candidate quant model.
  2. Run deterministic batches over each target Prompt Cohort. Use identical sampling seeds and temperature parameters.
  3. Collect metrics described below and compute Delta Metrics.
  4. Run a production-like serving simulation (see 'Serving Simulation' section) including batching and KV-cache warmup.

- Implementation notes: harness runs must be reproducible (git commit + artifact hash recorded). All runs produce an 'eval_manifest.json' with parameterized metadata: cohort, seed, runtime flags, hardware type.

Metrics and Thresholds

- Primary metrics (per-cohort):
  - fidelity_top1: top-1 correctness (classification/heavy QA), numeric exact-match or oracle score.
  - semantic_similarity: embedding-based cosine similarity on normalized outputs (mean).
  - response_latency_p50/p95: simulated response time with runtime batching.
  - sampling_stability: percentage of responses change beyond token-level edit-distance threshold.

- Cost metrics: peak_gpu_memory, tokens_per_second, expected_cost_per_1M_tokens.

- Threshold matrix (default):

  | Metric                 | Pass Threshold (per-cohort)         | Warning Delta | Fail Delta |
  | fidelity_top1          | >= baseline - 0.5%                  | -0.5% to -1.5% | <= -1.5% |
  | semantic_similarity    | >= baseline - 0.008 cosine          | -0.008 to -0.02 | <= -0.02 |
  | response_latency_p95   | <= baseline * 1.25                  | 1.25 to 1.5    | >=1.5   |
  | sampling_stability     | >= baseline - 1.0%                  | -1% to -3%     | <= -3%  |

- Aggregate decision rule: A Quant Candidate passes if no cohort shows a Fail Delta and at most one cohort shows a Warning Delta. Any Fail Delta triggers reject by default.

Serving Simulation and Runtime Guardrails

- Simulation must mimic production: target hardware (A100, H100, or CPU fallback), batch-size distribution sampled from production P50/P95, KV-cache warmup with representative prefix length per cohort.
- Guardrail configs to attach to candidate (example YAML-style table representation):

  | guardrail_name        | config_key                | default | intent |
  | max_input_tokens      | max_input_tokens          | 4096    | prevent OOM |
  | fallback_model        | fallback_model            | baseline_float | serve-quality fallback |
  | latency_slo_ms        | latency_slo_p95_ms        | 500     | trigger throttling |
  | kv_cache_threshold    | kv_cache_warmup_tokens    | 256     | ensure cache hits |

Canary and Rollout Procedure

1) Pre-canary gates (must be green): repository artifact signed, eval_manifest produced, passes AQEP decision rule, security scan clean.
2) Canary deploy: 1% traffic, 4hr window, cohorts instrumented with real-time eval probes.
3) Within canary: monitor live delta metrics, error rate, and estimated cost. If any cohort crosses Fail Delta -> immediate rollback (automated). If Warning Delta -> extend canary to 12 hours and run manual triage.
4) Progressive ramp: after 12hr of stable canary, move to 10% for 6hrs, 30% for 12hrs, 100% after 48hrs with continued monitoring.

Regression Triage Workflow

- Trigger: Canary fail or production alert tied to cohort-specific degradation.
- First responder: Applied ML oncall (first 30 min), Notify: SRE + Product metrics.
- Triage steps (numbered):
  1. Pull eval_manifest.json for candidate and baseline artifacts.
  2. Re-run Eval Harness for failing cohort(s) with higher sample density (N=500–2000 examples).
  3. Compare token-level diffs; flag systematic token drops/patterns (e.g., truncated completions, hallucination patterns).
  4. If deterministic regression reproduced, run targeted ablation: small-scale dequantize of last-n layers and re-evaluate.
  5. If ablation recovers metric, patch quant profile (e.g., raise precision for attention or FFN) and re-run full AQEP.
  6. If unrecoverable quickly, rollback candidate and open a Quant-Regression postmortem (owner: Applied ML).

Instrumentation and Observability

- Required telemetry emitted by runtime for quant candidates:
  - eval_cohort_id, request_id, model_variant, quant_profile_tag, p95_latency_ms, token_count, embedding_vector_id (if applicable), anomaly_flags.
- Dashboards: per-cohort fidelity and similarity timeseries, cost-per-token delta, and a canary summary panel showing active canaries and health.
- Alerts: automated alert if any cohort p95_fidelity drops by 1.0% vs baseline or if p95_latency increases by >50% during canary.

Example CLI snippets

- Run AQEP locally against candidate artifact:

  # run eval harness for selected cohorts
  redwood-eval harness run --artifact artifacts/q_candidate:v1 --cohorts short-instructions,code-completion-ml --seed 42 --hardware h100 --out eval_runs/q_candidate_manifest.json

- Promote candidate to canary (API example):

  curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
    -d '{"model_variant":"q_candidate:v1","traffic_percent":1,"canary_window_hours":4}' \
    https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/rollouts/promote

Decision Audit and Records

- Every run that contributes to an AQEP decision must be recorded in the model registry entry for the model with links to eval_manifest.json and canary logs.
- Maintain a short decision summary with: author, artifact_hash, cohorts_evaluated, pass/fail, and remediation notes. This summary is attached as 'quant_decision' metadata.

Ownership and Contacts

- Protocol owner: Applied ML (Priya Raman).
- Oncall responder: Applied ML oncall rotation (see /confluence/eng-sre/oncall-rotations).
- SRE contact for canary automation: Ethan Cole.

FAQ and Edge Cases

- Q: When should we hot-fix quantization for an existing production variant?
  A: Only if the regression is reproducible and impacts a critical cohort (high revenue/SLAs). Follow triage ablation steps and PR a new quant artifact.

- Q: How do we treat private deployments with slower telemetry?
  A: Use longer canary windows (default 24 hrs for private) and rely on exported eval probes collected via the private telemetry agent.

Appendix: Example Quant Profile Table (human readable)

  | profile_id | precision_scheme | special_layers | expected_mem_saving | recommended_for | notes |
  | q4f16-ld   | 4-bit (float16 emulation) | FFN:higher_prec | 2.4x                | short-instructions | fast, watch sampling |
  | q8-int8    | INT8 symmetric           | attention:8-bit   | 1.6x                | high-throughput     | robust on LLMs >=7B |
